title: Outlook: send local Word, Excel and PowerPoint files by email from the new Outlook for Windows
summary: Hold: the governance checklist mistakes a mailbox access setting for evidence that someone uses new Outlook. The claim that release-ring ordering is undocumented also overlooks Microsoft's published Targeted Release sequence; the roadmap facts, Message Center rollout windows and disabling commands are supported.

claims.quote: When working in an open Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file, users will now be able to send a copy of the locally stored file by email through the new Outlook for Windows.

claims.where: Scope: Rollout
claims.claim: New Outlook features are flighted to release rings and some tenants or users can enroll in Targeted Release.
claims.quote: New functionality is flighted to different release rings, as is the case for Microsoft 365 for the web. Some tenants or individual users in organizations could opt to get early access to features by enrolling in the Targeted release.

claims.where: Scope: Rollout; Open questions: release ring
claims.claim: Which release ring this feature uses, including whether Targeted Release comes first, is not stated.
claims.quote: In new Outlook, new features become available first in Targeted Release for 30 days and then are rolled out to Standard Release (General Availability).
claims.fix: Replace 'Which ring this feature uses is not stated' with 'Microsoft documents the general new Outlook sequence as Targeted Release for 30 days, then Standard Release (General Availability); MC1245222 gives General Availability windows but no feature-specific Targeted Release dates.' Replace the release-ring Open question with 'What are the feature-specific Targeted Release dates? MC1245222 does not give them.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/manage/manage-updates-new-outlook-windows.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: An admin UI for the specific per-mailbox OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled control is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled Exchange admin center user interface enable disable mailbox new Outlook. Opened enable-disable-employee-access-new-outlook and control-install; found PowerShell for this setting, not an admin UI.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell supports Set-CASMailbox -Identity <MailboxIdentity> -OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled $false to disable that mailbox's access in new Outlook.
claims.quote:
This example disables Outlook for Windows for the specified user.
Set-CASMailbox -Identity colin@contoso.onmicrosoft.com -OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled $false

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The mailbox-access control blocks new Outlook for that account, removing access to this feature there rather than disabling this feature alone.
claims.quote: their account is disabled in Outlook for Windows and they can no longer use Outlook for Windows with that account.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -Identity <PolicyIdentity> -OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled $false sets the equivalent access restriction per policy.
claims.quote:
To enable or disable access to mailboxes in Outlook for Windows in Outlook on the web mailbox policies, use the following syntax:
Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -Identity <PolicyIdentity> -OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled <$true | $false | $null>

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The policy setting affects all current and future mailboxes with that policy applied.
claims.quote: The value you specify in the Outlook on the web mailbox policy affects all current and future mailboxes that have the policy applied to them.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The access-control procedure points administrators to the Outlook on the web mailbox policies permissions entry.
claims.quote: To see what permissions you need, see the "Outlook on the web mailbox policies" entry in the Feature permissions in Exchange Online article.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled cmdlet parameter does not affect the Try the new Outlook toggle in classic Outlook.
claims.quote: The OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled parameter on the Set-CASMailbox or Set-OwaMailboxPolicy cmdlets doesn't affect the availability of the Try the new Outlook toggle in classic Outlook.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: Checking OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled identifies who uses new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: The default value for the OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled parameter on both cmdlets is blank ($null), which is equivalent to the value $true (users aren't restricted from accessing their work or school mailboxes using Outlook for Windows).
claims.fix: Replace the first Before rollout bullet with 'Review the OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled mailbox access setting (see the first controls row); Microsoft documents True or blank as access enabled.
